mainTopic: Using the צדדין of a tree on שבת, and preparing animal feed on שבת: extra effort on food (מיטרח באוכלא) versus making food (שוויי אוכלא)
overview: The amud opens at the end of a ברייתא about an עירוב placed in a basket hanging from a peg in a tree. The עירוב works only if the basket is below ten טפחים. The גמרא infers that without a peg the עירוב would fail, so this תנא seems to forbid using the 'sides' (צדדין) of a tree yet permit the 'sides of the sides' (צדי צדדין), against רבא. רב פפא answers that the no-peg case involves a tight basket, so taking the food shakes the tree itself. The הלכה is that צדדין are forbidden and צדי צדדין are permitted. רב אשי applies this to a ladder: lean it on pegs in the palm tree, and step only on the rungs. Then a new משנה deals with untying bundles of animal feed and crushing hay and carobs. רב הונא and רב יהודה define the bundles in opposite ways, based on opposite principles: may one put extra effort into food that is already edible, or may one turn something into food? The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the משנה twice. The first challenge is answered. The second ends in a קשיא, and a new proof begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא: a basket hung on a peg in a tree
steps.stepSummary: The end of a ברייתא: if someone stuck a peg in a tree and hung his עירוב basket on it, the עירוב is valid below ten טפחים but invalid above ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: [If someone drove] a peg into a tree and hung a basket on it: if it is above ten handbreadths, his עירוב is not a valid עירוב. If it is below ten handbreadths, his עירוב is a valid עירוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a ברייתא about an עירוב placed in a basket hanging from a peg in a tree. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above ten טפחים, the basket counts as a separate רשות היחיד, so the person standing below cannot take the food. That makes the עירוב invalid. Below ten, the food is reachable, and taking it from a basket on a peg is not direct use of the tree, so the עירוב works.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, עירוב תחומין: food set down to establish a new שבת 'home base'
Ten handbreadths, the height that creates a separate domain

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The ברייתא actually starts on the previous page with 'נעץ' (he drove a peg) before these words.

phrases.english: [drove] a peg into a tree and hung a basket on it.
phrases.notes: Continuation of the ברייתא from the previous page.

phrases.english: If above ten handbreadths —
his עירוב is not a valid עירוב.
If below ten handbreadths —
his עירוב is a valid עירוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage by quoting the source the גמרא will analyze.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A basket on a peg in a tree: the עירוב is valid below ten טפחים and invalid above ten.

steps.title: Inference: this תנא forbids sides but permits sides of sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that without a peg the עירוב would be invalid even below ten. That shows this תנא forbids צדדין but permits צדי צדדין, which challenges רבא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason [it works below ten] is that he drove a peg into the tree. But if he did not drive a peg, even below ten handbreadths his עירוב is not valid. So this תנא forbids [using] the sides, yet permits the sides of the sides!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads closely into the ברייתא and draws an inference that seems to contradict רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stresses the peg. That implies a basket tied straight to the tree would be forbidden, since taking from it is using the tree's 'sides' (צדדין). A basket on a peg is one step removed, the 'sides of the sides' (צדי צדדין), and that is allowed. So this תנא splits the two, forbidding צדדין but permitting צדי צדדין. That challenges רבא, who had treated them alike: whoever forbids צדדין also forbids צדי צדדין.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'sides' of a tree: something attached directly to it
The 'sides of the sides': something attached to something that is attached to the tree
But isn't it so that (introduces a challenge)

steps.confusionAlert: צדדין are things attached directly to the tree. צדי צדדין are one more step away, like a basket hanging on a peg that is stuck in the tree.

phrases.english: The reason is that he drove a peg into the tree,
but if he did not drive [a peg],
even below ten handbreadths
his עירוב is not a valid עירוב.
So this תנא forbids [using] the sides,
and permits the sides of the sides!
phrases.notes: Permitting צדי צדדין while forbidding צדדין contradicts רבא's view from the previous amud, which did not split the two.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנָעַץ יָתֵד בָּאִילָן, הָא לֹא נָעַץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the ברייתא in step 1 and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's opinion that one who forbids צדדין also forbids צדי צדדין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's focus on the peg implies a direct tie is forbidden while a peg is permitted. So the תנא forbids צדדין but permits צדי צדדין. רבא held that the two go together.

steps.title: רב פפא: a tight basket makes it direct use of the tree
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the no-peg case is a narrow basket tied tightly to the tree. Taking the food out shakes the tree, so it is using the tree itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are dealing with a tight basket. When he takes out the עירוב, he moves the tree, and so he is using the tree itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers by limiting the case to a specific kind of basket (an אוקימתא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a peg, the basket is narrow and pressed tightly against the tree. Pulling food out of it shakes the tree. That counts as using the tree itself, not merely its צדדין. So the ברייתא does not prove that this תנא forbids צדדין while permitting צדי צדדין, and it does not contradict רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with... (narrowing the case)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with a tight basket,
so that as he takes the עירוב —
he moves the tree,
and he is using the tree itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by defining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: אוקימתא: narrowing the case to a tightly tied, narrow basket
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forbidden no-peg case shows that this תנא forbids צדדין yet permits צדי צדדין, against רבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The no-peg case is forbidden because taking the food shakes the tree, which is direct use of the tree itself. So no prohibition of mere צדדין can be inferred, and the ברייתא does not contradict רבא.

steps.title: The הלכה: sides forbidden, sides of sides permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules: using צדדין of a tree is forbidden, but צדי צדדין are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: the sides are forbidden, and the sides of the sides are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling on this question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using something attached directly to a tree on שבת is forbidden. Using something one step further removed, like a basket hanging on a peg in the tree, is permitted. The ruling distinguishes between the two levels, as the plain reading of the ברייתא suggested.
steps.whatToRemember: צדדין אסורין, צדי צדדין מותרין: on שבת you may not use something attached directly to a tree, but you may use something attached to that attachment.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule for using trees on שבת, and רב אשי applies it right away in the next steps.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: the sides are forbidden,
the sides of the sides are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the issue raised in steps 2 and 3 with a final ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using צדדין of a tree on שבת is forbidden; using צדי צדדין is permitted.

steps.title: רב אשי: do not lean a ladder against the palm tree
steps.stepSummary: Based on the ruling, רב אשי says a ladder must not lean on the palm tree itself. Instead, it should lean on pegs sticking out from the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Now that you said the sides are forbidden, a ladder used to climb up should not be leaned against the palm tree, because that is using the sides. Rather, it should be leaned on the pegs that stick out from the palm tree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the new ruling and applies it to a common real-life case: a ladder near a palm tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaning a ladder directly on the tree makes the tree hold it up, which is using the tree's צדדין. Leaning it on pegs set into the tree is only צדי צדדין, which the הלכה just permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: Pegs or stakes sticking out from the tree

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Now that you said the sides are forbidden,
this ladder used to go up high —
a person should not lean it on the palm tree,
because that would be [using the] sides.
Rather, he should lean it on the pegs sticking out from the palm tree,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the halacha of step 4 to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ladder may not lean on the palm tree itself, only on pegs protruding from it.

steps.title: When climbing, step on the rungs, not the pegs
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that when climbing, a person should step only on the ladder's rungs, not on the pegs in the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he climbs, he should not put his foot on the pegs. Rather, he should put it on the rungs.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his practical instruction, explaining how to climb without breaking the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pegs are stuck directly into the tree, so they are the tree's צדדין. Stepping on them is forbidden. The rungs are part of the ladder, which only rests on the pegs, so they are צדי צדדין and permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: The pegs count as צדי צדדין when the ladder leans on them. But if your foot steps on them directly, you are using the tree's צדדין, so that is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: In practice: the ladder may lean on the pegs, but your feet may touch only the ladder.

phrases.english: And when he climbs —
he should not place his foot on the pegs,
rather he should place it on the rungs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's application from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When climbing, one steps only on the ladder's rungs and not on the pegs, which are the tree's צדדין.

steps.title: The new משנה: untying bundles and crushing feed for animals
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows untying פקיעין and spreading כיפין, but not זירין. It forbids crushing hay or carobs for any animal, though רבי יהודה allows crushing carobs for a small animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may untie bundles of grain in front of an animal. One may spread out the כיפין, but not the זירין. One may not crush hay or carobs in front of an animal, whether it is small or large. רבי יהודה allows crushing carobs for a small animal.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about preparing animal food on שבת. It lists what you may and may not do with bundles of feed, and with hay and carobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses three words for bundles: פקיעין, כיפין and זירין. It does not explain them, so the גמרא will need to define them. The ban on crushing shows there is a limit to how much effort you may put into preparing animal food on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreading apart or loosening a bundle
A type of bundle (defined in the גמרא)
Another type of bundle (defined in the גמרא)
Crushing or chopping into small pieces
A small animal / a large animal

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never tells us what כיפין and זירין are. Do not try to guess yet. The two opinions in the גמרא define these words in opposite ways.

phrases.english: Mishnah
One may untie bundles of grain before an animal,
and one may spread apart the kifin,
but not the zirin.
One may not crush the hay
nor the carobs before an animal,
whether for a small animal or for a large one.
Rabbi Yehuda permits it with carobs for a small animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מַתִּירִין פְּקִיעֵי עָמִיר לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It has no connection to the earlier tree and ladder discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may untie פקיעין and spread כיפין, but not זירין. Crushing hay or carobs is forbidden, except that רבי יהודה allows crushing carobs for a small animal.

steps.title: רב הונא defines the three bundle types
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says פקיעין and כיפין are the same kind of grain bundle. פקיעין are tied with two knots and כיפין with three. זירין are bundles of cedar branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: פקיעין and כיפין are the same thing. The difference is that פקיעין have two knots and כיפין have three. זירין are cedar bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה's terms. רב הונא gives his definitions first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, פקיעין and כיפין are both grain, which an animal can eat even while it is tied up. זירין are different: they are cedar branches, which an animal cannot eat while they are bundled.

keyTerms.meaning: They are the very same thing

phrases.english: Gemara
Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן פְּקִיעִין, הֵן הֵן כִּיפִין.
phrases.english: They are peki'in, and they are also kifin.
Peki'in have two knots, kifin have three;
zirin are bundles of cedar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֵן הֵן פְּקִיעִין, הֵן הֵן כִּיפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the bundle terms used in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פקיעין and כיפין are grain bundles (two or three knots). זירין are cedar bundles.

steps.title: רב הונא's reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: With his definitions, רב הונא reads the משנה this way: grain bundles may be untied and spread, but cedar bundles may neither be spread nor untied.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: you may untie grain bundles and spread them, and the same is true for כיפין. But זירין may be neither spread nor untied.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא now rereads the משנה using his definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פקיעין and כיפין are the same grain, both may be untied and spread. זירין are fully forbidden; you may not even untie them.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it means

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
One may untie bundles of grain before an animal,
and spread them.
And the same is true for kifin,
but not the zirin:
neither to spread nor to untie.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: מַתִּירִין פְּקִיעֵי עָמִיר לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה, וּמְפַסְפְסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב הונא's definitions to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain bundles may be untied and spread. Cedar bundles may be neither untied nor spread.

steps.title: רב חסדא explains רב הונא's reason
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that רב הונא allows extra effort on food that is already edible. But he forbids turning something into food on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: What is רב הונא's reason? He holds that we may put effort into food, but we may not make something into food.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gives the principle behind רב הונא's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain is already edible, so untying and spreading it is only extra effort, and that is allowed. Cedar branches cannot be eaten while bundled. Untying them would create food, and that is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: To put effort into something that is already food

steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is what the challenges in steps 14 and 18 attack.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא קָא סָבַר
phrases.english: What is Rav Huna's reason? He holds:
to exert oneself with food, we may exert ourselves;
to make something into food, we may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב הונא's reading.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Effort on food is allowed. Making something into food is forbidden.

steps.title: רב יהודה defines the bundle types differently
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says פקיעין and זירין are the same kind of bundle. פקיעין have two knots and זירין have three. כיפין are the cedar bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: פקיעין and זירין are the same thing. The difference is that פקיעין have two knots and זירין have three. כיפין are cedar bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, opposite set of definitions from רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה switches the roles. Now זירין are the grain bundles, and כיפין are the cedar bundles. This changes how the whole משנה reads.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who disagrees with רב הונא here

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה (the אמורא here) with רבי יהודה (the תנא in the משנה who allows crushing carobs). They are different people.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן פְּקִיעִין, הֵן הֵן זִירִין.
phrases.english: They are peki'in, and they are also zirin.
Peki'in have two knots, zirin have three;
kifin are bundles of cedar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: הֵן הֵן פְּקִיעִין, הֵן הֵן זִירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives definitions opposite to רב הונא's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פקיעין and זירין are grain bundles. כיפין are cedar bundles.

steps.title: רב יהודה's reading of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reads the משנה this way: grain bundles (פקיעין and זירין) may be untied but not spread. Cedar bundles (כיפין) may even be spread.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: you may untie grain bundles in front of an animal, but not spread them. כיפין may even be spread. But זירין may not be spread, only untied.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה rereads the משנה using his definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain bundles get only the minimum: untying, but no spreading. Cedar bundles, which cannot be eaten without being opened up, may be both untied and spread.

phrases.english: And this is what it is saying:
One may untie bundles of grain before an animal,
but spreading them, no;
and kifin, we may also spread them;
but not the zirin,
to spread, only to untie.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: מַתִּירִין פְּקִיעֵי עָמִיר לִפְנֵי בְּהֵמָה, אֲבָל פַּסְפּוֹסֵי — לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רב יהודה's definitions to the wording of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain bundles may be untied but not spread. Cedar bundles may also be spread.

steps.title: רבא explains רב יהודה's reason
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב יהודה holds the opposite of רב הונא. Turning something into food is allowed, but extra effort on food that is already edible is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רב יהודה's reason? He holds that we may make something into food, but we may not put extra effort into food.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the principle behind רב יהודה's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cedar must be opened up to become food, so spreading it is allowed. Grain is already edible once untied, so spreading it is unnecessary extra effort and is forbidden. This is the exact reverse of רב הונא's principle.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: effort on food is allowed, making food is forbidden. רב יהודה: making food is allowed, effort on food is forbidden.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is Rav Yehuda's reason? He holds:
making something into food, we may do;
exerting ourselves with food, we may not.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב יהודה's reading, the reverse of רב חסדא's explanation of רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making something into food is allowed. Extra effort on food is forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge to רב הונא from the ban on crushing soft carobs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids crushing hay and carobs. If the carobs are soft like hay, they are already edible, so crushing them is only extra effort. That shows extra effort is forbidden, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one may not crush hay or carobs in front of an animal, whether small or large. Doesn't this mean carobs that are like hay? Just as hay is soft, these carobs are soft too. So we see that we may not put effort into food. This is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the second part of the משנה to attack רב הונא's principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soft hay and soft carobs can already be eaten as they are, so crushing them is only extra effort. Yet the משנה forbids it. That contradicts רב הונא's rule that extra effort on food is allowed.

phrases.english: We learned:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְרַסְּקִין אֶת הַשַּׁחַת וְאֶת הֶחָרוּבִין
phrases.english: One may not crush hay or carobs
before an animal,
whether small or large.
Is it not that the carobs are like the hay:
just as hay is soft,
so too the carobs are soft.
Apparently, we do not exert ourselves with food,
and this is a refutation of Rav Huna!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: אֵין מְרַסְּקִין אֶת הַשַּׁחַת וְאֶת הֶחָרוּבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה to attack רב הונא's principle, which in turn supports רב יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's principle (as explained by רב חסדא) that extra effort on edible food is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Soft carobs and hay are already edible, so crushing them is only extra effort. The משנה forbids it, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: רב הונא: The hay in the משנה is hard like the carobs
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה speaks about hard hay, like hard carobs. Crushing it makes it edible, so it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא can answer you: No. The hay is like the carobs. Just as the carobs are hard, so too the hay is hard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge from step 14. He says the משנה is not talking about soft carobs at all. It is talking about hard hay and hard carobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed the carobs were soft like hay, so crushing them was only extra effort. רב הונא flips the comparison. The hay is hard like the carobs, so crushing turns it into food (שוויי אוכלא), which רב הונא also forbids. So the משנה fits his view.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 14 the carobs were compared to the hay (חרובין דומיא דשחת) to make the carobs 'soft'. Here it is reversed: the hay is compared to the carobs (שחת דומיא דחרובין) to make the hay 'hard'. Same comparison, opposite direction.

phrases.english: Rav Huna can say to you: No,
the hay is similar to the carobs:
just as the carobs are ones that are hard,
so too the hay is hay that is hard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by redefining the case in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the hay is hard, not soft.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The carobs were soft like hay, so crushing them was only extra effort, and the משנה forbids it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hay is hard like carobs, so crushing it turns it into food. This is forbidden even according to רב הונא.

steps.title: When is hay so hard that it cannot be eaten?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how there could be hay that is too hard for an animal to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you find such a case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about רב הונא's answer. Animals usually eat hay easily, so when is hay 'hard'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's answer only works if there really is hay that an animal cannot eat without crushing. The גמרא wants a real-life case. This is a clarifying question, not an attack.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you find it? (asking for a real case)

phrases.english: How can you find it (such hay)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a practical example of the 'hard hay' that step 15 introduced.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where hay is too hard for an animal to eat without crushing.

steps.title: Hay for young donkeys
steps.stepSummary: The case is young donkeys, who can only eat hay that has been crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: With young donkeys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case is young donkeys. For them, uncrushed hay counts as 'hard'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young donkeys cannot chew regular hay well. For them, crushing the hay is what turns it into food. That is a case of שוויי אוכלא, so רב הונא's reading of the משנה works.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the first challenge: the משנה forbids crushing because the hay and carobs are hard, so crushing would make them into food.

phrases.english: With young donkeys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Hay given to young donkeys, who cannot eat it unless it is crushed.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יהודה permitting carobs for a small animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה allows crushing carobs for a small animal but not a large one. This only makes sense if the תנא קמא forbids extra effort, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יהודה permits crushing carobs for a small animal. For a small one, yes; for a large one, no. It makes sense if the תנא קמא holds that we may not put extra effort into food but we may make food edible. Then רבי יהודה is saying that carobs for a small animal are also a case of making food edible. But if the תנא קמא holds that we may not make food edible but we may put extra effort into food, then if רבי יהודה permits carobs for a small animal, he should surely permit them for a large one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge to רב הונא from the next part of the משנה. It reads רבי יהודה's words closely to show what the תנא קמא must hold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה permits crushing carobs only for a small animal, not for a large one. If the תנא קמא allows making food but forbids extra effort, this fits: רבי יהודה is saying that for a small animal, crushing carobs is also making food. But if the תנא קמא forbids making food and allows extra effort (רב הונא's view), then רבי יהודה's permission must mean the small animal can already eat the carobs, so crushing is only extra effort. In that case a large animal, which eats carobs even more easily, should surely be allowed too. Since רבי יהודה does not allow it for a large animal, רב הונא's reading is challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source used as proof or challenge)
Small animal (like a goat or sheep)
The first, anonymous opinion in the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is the one permitting here. But the proof is about what the תנא קמא holds, based on the exact way רבי יהודה answers him.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Yehuda permits crushing carobs for a small animal.
For a small animal, yes; for a large animal, no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא infers this from the wording.

phrases.english: It makes sense if you say
that the first tanna holds:
we do not put extra effort into food,
but making it into food, we may make,
that explains what Rabbi Yehuda is saying:
carobs for a small animal are also
a case of making something into food.
But if you say
that the first tanna holds
we may not make something into food,
but we may put extra effort into food,
then if Rabbi Yehuda permits carobs for a small animal,
all the more so for a large animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מַתִּיר בֶּחָרוּבִין לַדַּקָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב הונא answered the first challenge, a second challenge is brought from the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that extra effort on edible food is allowed but making food is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב הונא, permitting carobs for a small animal would mean a large animal is surely allowed. רבי יהודה's limit to a small animal only fits the view that making food is allowed and extra effort is forbidden.

steps.title: דקה means a large animal that is picky about food
steps.stepSummary: The word דקה does not mean a small animal. It means a large animal that is picky (דייקא) about its food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think 'דקה' means a truly small animal? What does 'דקה' mean? A large animal. And why is it called 'דקה'? Because it is picky about its food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the word דקה differently. It is a large animal, called דקה because it is picky (דייקא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה is talking about a large animal that could eat the carobs uncrushed when it has to, then crushing is only extra effort. רבי יהודה allows this, which fits רב הונא. The challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think...? (introduces a rejection of an assumption)

phrases.english: Do you think 'daka' means an actual small animal?
What is 'daka'? A large animal,
and why does it call it 'daka'?
Because it is picky about its food.
phrases.notes: A play on words: דקה (small) / דייקא (picky).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by reinterpreting the word דקה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דקה means a small animal that truly cannot eat the carobs, so crushing makes food.
steps.terutzMaskana: דקה means a picky large animal, so crushing is only extra effort, which רבי יהודה allows, in line with רב הונא.

steps.title: The first clause shows דקה means a truly small animal — left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The first clause of the משנה says 'whether דקה or גסה', which shows דקה means a really small animal. The גמרא has no answer: קשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the first part teaches 'whether for a small animal or for a large animal', it shows that רבי יהודה meant 'דקה' as an actual small animal! This is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 19. The first part of the משנה uses דקה next to גסה, so it must mean a truly small animal. The question stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause דקה is set against גסה, so it clearly means 'small'. רבי יהודה is responding to that clause, so his דקה should mean the same. The גמרא cannot answer and ends with 'קשיא', a difficulty that is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from רבי יהודה ends with 'קשיא', an unresolved difficulty. A קשיא leaves a question open, but it is weaker than a full refutation (תיובתא). So רב הונא's view is not fully rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: 'קשיא' at the end of a sugya does not mean the opinion was knocked down. It means the question was left open. A full refutation would be called 'תיובתא'.

phrases.english: But from the fact that the first clause teaches:
'whether for a small animal or for a large animal',
it can be inferred that Rabbi Yehuda,
when he said 'daka', meant an actual small animal!
It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reinterpretation of step 19 and returns the challenge of step 18 to full force.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading in step 19 that דקה means a picky large animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first clause pairs דקה with גסה, so דקה must mean small. רבי יהודה's דקה should mean the same thing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge against רב הונא from רבי יהודה remains unanswered (קשיא), but it is not a full refutation.

steps.title: Opening a new proof from a source about chopping
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says 'come and hear' and starts quoting a source that permits chopping food. It will use this source to test whether extra effort to prepare animal food is allowed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a proof from another source: 'One may chop...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move by bringing a new source as evidence. The quote has only just begun, so the actual proof comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier challenge from רבי יהודה ended in a קשיא with no answer. Now the גמרא tries a different source, one that permits chopping. Chopping is work that makes food easier to eat, so this source should help decide whether extra effort for an animal's food is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One may chop' or 'one may cut up.' The first word of the source being quoted.

steps.confusionAlert: This step stops in the middle of a quote. Do not try to draw a conclusion from 'מחתכין' alone. Wait for the rest of the source and the גמרא's reasoning on the next amud.

phrases.english: Come and hear: One may chop
phrases.notes: 'תא שמע' opens a new proof. 'מחתכין' is the first word of the quoted source, and the quote continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The previous attempt ended in an unanswered קשיא. The גמרא now brings a fresh source to examine the same question about extra effort.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one may go to extra effort to prepare animal food on שבת, the question connected to רב הונא's view.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source that begins 'מחתכין' (one may chop). Its full text continues on the next amud.
